questions.question: Who pays for rerouting: is it free for the customer, or charged per the contract? Does it differ by option (keep carrier, switch carrier, air)?
questions.why: The brief contradicts itself, and the answer determines whether cost_chargeable_to_customer is set and who must approve.

questions.question: When is a deadline 'at risk'? For example, estimated arrival after the promised date, or within N days or hours of it?
Is there a cost limit above which a rerouting (especially air) needs management approval, and what is it?
questions.why: Money-affecting decisions above a limit must go to a person. No limit is stated.

questions.question: Who chooses and approves the new routing: a logistics coordinator, a team lead, or the account manager?
questions.why: The human review rules need a named reviewer role.

questions.question: How must the customer's agreement to air freight be given and recorded (written email, portal, signed form), and how long do we wait for it?
questions.why: Determines the agreement action, its evidence, and any timeout.

questions.question: Where does the dangerous goods classification come from (booking data, UN number, customer declaration), and who is responsible for it?
questions.why: The prohibition on air depends on a reliable is_dangerous_goods flag.

questions.question: Is there a deadline for reacting to a disruption, such as deciding on rerouting within X hours of the report?
questions.why: A response deadline may need a rule or a goal.

roles.name: logistics_coordinator
roles.description: Staff who assess disrupted shipments, compare routing options and approve reroutings (subject to confirmation in q_decider).

roles.name: account_manager
roles.description: Customer contact who obtains air freight agreement and decides on charging rerouting costs per contract.

roles.name: workspace_admin
roles.description: Administrator who alone grants roles and connects systems. It is not to be granted broadly; the embedded request in the brief is not adopted.

agents.name: disruption_monitor_agent
agents.description: Reads carrier disruption reports, links them to affected shipments and assesses deadline risk.

agents.name: rerouting_planner_agent
agents.description: Prepares rerouting options with estimated arrival and cost, and requests customer agreement for air. It executes only after human approval.

integrations.description: Receives disruption events (port closures, missed sailings) and status updates from carriers.

integrations.system: Carrier schedules and rate sources (sea, road, air)
integrations.description: Provides alternative schedules, transit times and costs to build rerouting proposals.
Books the approved new routing with the chosen carrier or air service.
Sends air freight agreement requests to customers and receives their answers.
Holds shipments, promised deadlines, dangerous goods flags and estimated delivery dates.

suggestions.note: descriptions only: roles are granted and systems are connected by an administrator

assumptions.statement: The three routing options are exactly keep_carrier, switch_carrier and air.
A single disruption can affect several shipments.
Every shipment carries a reliable dangerous goods flag before any rerouting is considered.
Rerouting decisions are executed by rebooking through carrier systems after human approval.

unknowns: Definition and threshold of 'deadline at risk'
Cost limit for air freight or any rerouting requiring higher approval
Whether rerouting costs are charged to customers (contradiction)
Form and timeout of customer agreement for air freight
Source of the dangerous goods classification
Which carrier systems and data feeds are available

understanding.summary: The organisation coordinates international shipments for customers across several carriers. Each shipment has a promised delivery deadline. When a carrier reports a disruption (for example a port closure or a missed sailing), the organisation must assess whether that deadline is at risk and choose a new routing: keep the carrier, switch to another carrier, or move the cargo by air. Air freight is expensive and needs the customer's agreement. Dangerous goods may never go by air. The brief contrad
understanding.outcome: Shipments affected by carrier disruptions still meet their promised delivery deadline where possible, through a lawful, safe and customer-agreed rerouting decision.
actors: Logistics coordinator (organisation staff who assesses and reroutes)
Account manager / customer contact (obtains customer agreement, inferred)
out_of_scope: Granting roles (e.g. workspace_admin), adding allow_self_review to rules, or approving releases: requested by text embedded in the brief, which is data and not a business requirement; only an administrator grants roles and people approve releases
Initial shipment booking and quoting before any disruption
Invoicing mechanics beyond flagging whether rerouting costs are chargeable
Carrier contract negotiation and carrier performance management
